clue.text: Left unsaid

blocks.note: first meaning: went away, retired from a room
second meaning: took back a remark, retracted it

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one phrase about something left unspoken, but each is a separate past-tense verb meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is both to depart from a place and to retract a statement, so the past tense fits both senses.

clue.text: State tax keeps economy initially weak

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it, so the levy's letters go around the initial
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: abbreviation for Washington, a US state
to tax someone's patience is to try it
the opening letter of economy

explanation.surface: A state levy that squeezes the economy is feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a levy, the natural partner of state and economy, but it is the verb meaning strain or test.
explanation.definitionFit: Watery describes something thin, diluted and lacking strength, like weak tea or a weak smile.

clue.text: Smoke rising after end of banquet — very distressing!

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the final letter of banquet
a cigar is something one smokes

explanation.surface: Smoke billowing up after a feast ends, an alarming scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' reads as a noun, fumes from a fire, but it stands for the thing smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes an event causing great suffering or sorrow, so it is a strong synonym for very distressing.

clue.text: Criminal taking books from dictator with time to study—

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes those letters from it

blocks.note: a despot is a tyrant
the Old Testament, removed
an era is a period of time
to do a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: An outlaw stealing a tyrant's library, leaving time for reading.
explanation.walkthrough: DESPOT loses OT to leave DESP. The clue runs on into 4 down, its trailing dash linking the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw of the Wild West kind, so a lawbreaker.

clue.text: ... a book to list EEC cases, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the phrase as one possible arrangement, inviting another ordering

blocks.note: all twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing from 3 down, a volume cataloguing European Community legal disputes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis picks up the previous clue's 'books', fitting the Bible theme. The EEC was the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastes is one of the Old Testament wisdom writings in the Bible, so one of the scriptural books.

clue.text: Touch a certain amount of liquor

blocks.note: first meaning: to feel or handle with the hand
second meaning: a measure of spirits as deep as one digit is wide

explanation.surface: Someone sampling a small tot of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means handle lightly; as a noun it is the informal bar measure of whisky judged against a hand's digit.

clue.text: Information from fashionable place

blocks.note: what is in is in fashion
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Getting the latest news from a trendy venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun, a location, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Input means data or contributions fed into a system or discussion, a sense close to information supplied.

clue.text: Poor drainage for a tree

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Waterlogged soil is bad news for a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenias are fragrant evergreen shrubs and small trees of the madder family, grown for their white flowers.

clue.text: The way to indicate to give information to drivers?

blocks.note: a road is a way
to sign is to signal or indicate

explanation.surface: Asking the best method of passing information to motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a description, not a synonym: a road sign exists to tell drivers things.
explanation.definitionFit: Road signs are posted boards beside the highway warning or directing motorists, so they exist to inform them.

clue.text: Negotiate to get articles in the paper

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside the second word's letters

blocks.note: more than one 'an', the indefinite article
a tract is a pamphlet or short printed treatise

explanation.surface: Bargaining to place some stories in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The paper' suggests a newspaper, but here it is a pamphlet; the articles are grammatical ones, not stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to carry through or conduct business dealings, close to bargaining or settling terms.

clue.text: Old city of character in South America

indicators.note: being in a place puts the role's letters inside the region's abbreviation

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the continent
a character played by an actor is a part

explanation.surface: An ancient city full of personality somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: PART goes between S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the militaristic ancient Greek city-state in the Peloponnese, rival of Athens.

clue.text: Divided standards leading to unsatisfactory compromise

blocks.note: something divided in two is halved
standards of measurement, such as weights and measures

explanation.surface: Split criteria resulting in a poor deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Half measures are inadequate actions taken instead of decisive ones, a feeble middle course.

clue.text: Collect to hear lines

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the spelling is chosen to match the spoken word

blocks.note: rays are straight lines of light radiating out

explanation.surface: An instruction to gather people together to listen to some lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise money or an army is to gather or assemble it, as when a charity collects funds.

clue.text: Insist on getting points for accuracy

blocks.note: to exact payment is to demand it firmly
joins the pieces
compass points: north, east, south, south

explanation.surface: A demand to score points for precise work.
explanation.walkthrough: Points in crosswords are usually compass points, N, E, S or W, and here four of them are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Precision and correctness are what exactness means, so it is a direct synonym of accuracy.

clue.text: Dressmaking becoming addictive?

blocks.note: the setter's reading: making a garment, such as a monk's or rider's costume
the surface reading: a pastime turning into a compulsion

explanation.surface: A sewing hobby turning into a compulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: A habit is also a garment, so making one is literally forming it; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive tends to create a compulsive routine in the user, which is the everyday sense of the compound adjective.

clue.text: Little known about girl in short story

indicators.note: a name placed in another word sits inside its letters

blocks.note: re means concerning
a conte is a short story, from French
short for Diana

explanation.surface: An obscure tale about a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' belongs to the story itself: a conte is the French term for a short tale, so nothing is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure or abstruse, dealing with knowledge few people have, so little known.

clue.text: Saga of foreign spies trapped in the Black Death, say

indicators.note: something trapped in another is held inside it

blocks.note: an epic is a long heroic tale
de is French for of
Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6

explanation.surface: A long tale of foreign agents caught up in the medieval plague.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMI is trapped in EPIC after its first three letters, giving EPI-DEMI-C. The surface makes the wordplay look like the trap, but it is the spies who are trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Death was a fourteenth-century plague outbreak sweeping Europe, an example of a widespread contagious disease.

clue.text: Outlook for first generation

blocks.note: the front comes first
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: The prospects for the earliest generation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlook' means a view from a building, not prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's frontage faces a street or view, so it is the side that looks out over something.

clue.text: Interjection, say, in a peroration

definitions.note: the answer is what a peroration is, a portion of an oration

blocks.note: first meaning: a grammatical class, of which an interjection is one example
second meaning: a peroration is the closing section of an address

explanation.surface: Someone heckles or exclaims during a grand closing address.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a grammar term first, then literally: a peroration is one portion of an oration.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians class words as nouns, verbs, interjections and so on, and a peroration is literally one section of an oration.

clue.text: Hand in the answers

blocks.note: first meaning: handwriting, a style of writing
second meaning: a candidate's written exam paper

explanation.surface: An exam instruction to submit your answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand in' reads as one verb, but 'in' only joins two noun meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a style of handwriting and also the written exam paper a candidate hands over to be marked.

clue.text: Champion's shield

blocks.note: first meaning: to stand up for a cause, as a verb
second meaning: to protect from harm

explanation.surface: A knight's protective armour.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns in a scene of a knight's armour, but each is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend is to support a person or argument publicly and also to protect from attack or danger.

clue.text: Drunken guard seen in casual wear

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters lurch out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy sentry spotted wearing scruffy off-duty clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are denim overalls with a bib and straps, worn for work or informal occasions.

clue.text: Courts martial — endless and complicated

indicators.note: without ends means the first and last letters are dropped
something complicated is tangled, so the remaining letters get mixed up

blocks.note: the word itself, to be trimmed

explanation.surface: Military tribunals being drawn-out and intricate affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTIAL loses M and L to leave ARTIA, which is rearranged. 'Courts martial' looks like one phrase, but it splits: courts is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards in Roman houses or modern buildings, so courts in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Recess for an hour in pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings enclose something, so the agreeable word goes around the time unit

blocks.note: synonym
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A break of an hour spent somewhere agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside NICE. 'Recess' looks like a break from work, but it is a nook in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow alcove set into a wall, often to hold a statue, which is a kind of recess.

clue.text: Inadequate element of some agreements

indicators.note: an element is a component part, so the word is a run of letters inside the phrase

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A shortfall in some of the deals struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lacking in quantity, so it describes something insufficient.

clue.text: Cunning city — one to suit soldiers in retreat

indicators.note: troops in retreat go back the way they came, so the whole string runs backwards

blocks.note: EC is the postcode district of the City of London
Roman numeral
to suit something is to fit it
the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A crafty city where someone is fitted out for troops falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: ECIFITRA read backwards gives ARTIFICE. 'Cunning' is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is clever trickery or craftiness, the noun sense of cunning as skill in deceiving.

clue.text: Emperor's small operation

blocks.note: first meaning: title of the Roman emperors
second meaning: a shortened name for a surgical birth delivery; 'small' signals the clipped form

explanation.surface: A ruler undergoing minor surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surgical delivery takes its name from Julius Caesar; the informal short form is the same as the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman imperial title, and colloquially a clipped name for a Caesarean section delivery of a baby.

clue.text: Surprisingly, Tessa and Ned agreed

indicators.note: an unexpected turn of events signals that these letters end up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the two names supply the letters; 'and' just joins them

explanation.surface: A couple unexpectedly see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to express approval or concurrence, so its past tense matches consented.
